witness_description: On vertices {0,1,2}, take the triangle with weights w(0,1)=1, w(0,2)=1, and w(1,2)=2. Its unique minimum spanning tree is {{0,1},{0,2}}, so edge {0,1} belongs to every minimum spanning tree. Removing {0,1} leaves the path 0-2-1 connected, so {0,1} is not a bridge.
refutation_explanation: The conclusion requires the edge to be a bridge (in particular, before it can be a minimum-weight bridge). The exhibited edge belongs to every minimum spanning tree but is not a bridge, so it violates the implication.
search_space: All 68 encodings of labeled simple undirected graphs on n in {2,3}, where every possible edge is independently absent or has integer weight in {1,2,3}; every encoding was visited in fixed lexicographic product order, and minimum spanning trees were exhaustively enumerated for each connected encoding.
